hook: The former KGB officer who has ruled Russia since 1999.

pages.x: Vladimir Putin was born in Leningrad, now St Petersburg, in 1952, and grew up in a shared flat. An older brother he never knew had died during the wartime siege of the city. As a boy he took up judo.

After studying law he joined the KGB, the Soviet secret police and spy service, and in the 1980s was posted to Dresden in East Germany. When the Berlin Wall fell in 1989, he burned files as crowds gathered outside.

He worked for the mayor of St Petersburg, then in Moscow, and in 1998 became head of the FSB, the successor of the KGB. In 1999 President Yeltsin made him prime minister, then resigned on New Year's Eve, leaving Putin in charge.
He led a brutal second war in Chechnya, in which the city of Grozny was largely destroyed.

Living standards rose with oil money in his first years. Independent television was taken over, opponents were jailed or driven abroad, and several prominent critics were murdered or died in prison; the Kremlin denies any part in their deaths.
A black belt in judo, he has been shown on state television riding a horse bare-chested, flying with cranes and diving to find ancient jars, which turned out to have been planted.
In 2014 Russia seized Crimea from Ukraine and annexed it.

In 2020 the constitution was changed so that he could stay in power until 2036. In February 2022 he launched a full invasion of Ukraine, the largest war in Europe since 1945. The International Criminal Court has issued a warrant for his arrest.
Putin has ruled Russia longer than anyone since Stalin. He restored Russian power after the chaos of the 1990s, but turned the country into an authoritarian state and led it into war with Ukraine.
pts: Launched the invasion of Ukraine in 2022
